claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a fine nanocrystalline microstructure.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating contains minimal pre-formed oxide.
During high-temperature sliding, an oxide layer forms in situ on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
The in situ oxide layer is thin, adherent, and nanocrystalline.
The oxide layer is enriched in Cr and Cu oxides.
Formation of the oxide layer governs the overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation of the coating at high temperature.
Annealing at 600°C for one hour in air promotes oxidation of Cr and Cu in the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Selective oxidation of Cr and Cu at elevated temperature creates an adherent oxide tribolayer.
The oxide tribolayer distributes applied stress and acts as a load-bearing barrier during sliding.
The oxide tribolayer limits surface dislocation nucleation and localized plastic shear.
The annealed coating will have a lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating during sliding at approximately 600°C.
The annealed coating will exhibit a more uniform and spatially distributed microscopic deformation pattern than the as-deposited coating.
The predicted wear and deformation effects are restricted to high-temperature sliding near 600°C under comparable loads and sliding speeds.

contradictions.description: The governing layer is described as forming in situ during sliding, but the intervention is an air anneal intended to oxidize the coating before sliding. It is therefore unclear whether the predicted benefit is attributed to a pre-formed annealing oxide or to an oxide generated during the wear test.
